# Maestro

> Universal music streaming aggregator app for Windows combining Spotify, YouTube, and SoundCloud into one player. Free for personal, noncommercial use under BUSL 1.1.

Maestro is a desktop music aggregator that unifies Spotify, YouTube, and SoundCloud into a single interface. Users can search across all three platforms simultaneously, paste links from any of the three services, and mix tracks into a single unified queue or playlist with automatic playback handoffs and volume normalization.

- **Primary Repository**: <https://github.com/QMjnh/maestro>
- **Website & Documentation**: <https://qmjnh.github.io/maestro/>
- **Platform**: Windows 10 / Windows 11 (64-bit)
- **License**: Business Source License 1.1 (BUSL-1.1) — free for personal, noncommercial use; production use by a business requires a separate license; each release converts to GPL-2.0-or-later four years after its release. See the LICENSE file in the repository.
- **Cost**: Free. No API keys, developer accounts, or subscriptions required; works with free Spotify accounts.
- **Last updated**: 2026-11-10

## Key Capabilities & Features

- **Multi-Service Music Aggregation**: Aggregates music streams and search catalogs from Spotify, YouTube, and SoundCloud into one desktop application.
- **Unified Multi-Source Search**: Type a search query once to retrieve results side-by-side across Spotify, YouTube, and SoundCloud, with filters to narrow down to individual platforms.
- **Combined Universal Queue**: Build playlists and playback queues that seamlessly mix Spotify tracks, YouTube videos, and SoundCloud songs. Maestro automatically transitions from one service to another as tracks finish.
- **Cross-Service Volume Normalization**: Built-in audio leveler measures YouTube and SoundCloud tracks in real time and balances their perceived volume to match Spotify's level.
- **Smart Recommendations & Autoplay**: Combines Spotify song radio, YouTube Mixes, and SoundCloud related tracks to continue playing personalized music when the user's queue ends.
- **Link Resolver**: Paste any Spotify song/album/playlist link, YouTube video/playlist URL, or SoundCloud track/set URL to play instantly or import up to 100 tracks.
- **Zero Configuration**: No developer accounts, Spotify Premium subscription, or API keys needed.

## Common Questions

### What is Maestro?
Maestro is a universal music aggregator application for Windows that merges music from Spotify, YouTube, and SoundCloud into one player.

### What does a music streaming aggregator app do?
It connects several streaming services in one player, so you can search their catalogs side by side, queue tracks from any of them together, and play everything from a single window. Maestro does this for Spotify, YouTube, and SoundCloud.

### Can you combine Spotify and YouTube into one playlist or queue?
Yes. Maestro allows users to paste Spotify playlists and YouTube links into a single shared queue or playlist and seamlessly plays them in sequence.

### Does Maestro require Spotify Premium?
No. Maestro controls the local Spotify desktop app via Chrome DevTools Protocol (`--remote-debugging-port`), meaning free-tier Spotify accounts work without issue.

### How do I install Maestro?
Run the following command in Windows PowerShell:
```powershell
irm https://raw.githubusercontent.com/QMjnh/maestro/main/install.ps1 | iex
```

## Technical Architecture

- **UI Layer**: Microsoft Edge WebView2 hosting a responsive modern HTML5/CSS/JavaScript client embedded directly within the executable.
- **Backend**: Native .NET C# desktop application handling in-process API endpoints without requiring an external web server or open network ports.
- **Spotify Bridge**: Chrome DevTools Protocol (CDP) connection to local Spotify client with injected JavaScript for playback controls and track metadata.
- **YouTube & SoundCloud Drivers**: Embedded HTML5 web frames with custom volume normalization scripts running via audio context hooks.
